title: Small regular Seiberg–Witten perturbations without irreducible solutions on Solv rational homology three-spheres with sufficiently small torus fibres
author: Francesco Lin
work: Monopole Floer homology and SOLV geometry
source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue 3 (2020), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/ahl.56
difficulty_reason: The proof combines nonabelian Fourier analysis on Solv lattices with a borderline coexact spectral criterion, identifies spin structures through torus-semibundle covers, and controls Dirac kernels to achieve regularity while excluding irreducible monopoles. This geometric gauge-theoretic argument exceeds ordinary qualifying exams.

primary_locator.required_core: complete source Solv lattice/Fourier, coexact-spectrum, perturbed-monopole compactness and harmonic Dirac/spin-cover arguments

source_scope_note: The selected problem is Theorem 1.1: existence of small regular Seiberg--Witten perturbations without irreducible solutions, for a Solv rational homology three-sphere equipped with a sufficiently small-fibre Solv metric. The complete author body retains all local double-cover/lattice, Fourier, coexact-spectrum, borderline compactness/equality, harmonic Dirac and spin-cover arguments and final transversality. No arbitrary-metric or arbitrary-perturbation assertion is selected; L-space consequences remain uncounted context.
